Got my washer to spin again - My Whirlpool washer Model LSR6132HQ1 finally quit after 20 years. It wouldn't spin on any rinse cycle that I set in the timer. I pulled out the lid switch and found it had disintegrated with age. With 2 phillip screws, I was able to remove it for inspection. Another 4 screws on the washer bulkhead and I had access to replace the switch & wiring. (quite a few videos on You-tube on how to do this.) It took less then an hour to do it taking my time & cleaning up washer grime & dust,etc. I didn't purchase the high marked up $38 OEM switch but decided on this $8 switch. Comparing both, they looked identical and wouldn't be surprised if they were made in the same factory. The switch "clicks" when depressed and works properly. Wife is happy, I'm happy, and we saved a $150 service call with just a phillips screwdriver. We are going out for dinner!

Anyway, my beloved Nespresso is closeted, for now, and I'm using Illy Forte K cups. The resulting coffee is fine, smooth actually, and provides a passable espresso, but it's not up to my Nespresso espresso. I'd be fine with that, except that Nespresso (and a few others, like Peets) are made of recyclable aluminum and these companies actually give you a free postage packet to return the used pods. Which is probably why they cost 70-75 cents per cup, and I have to buy online.

So, hating to add to the waste stream with these plastic k cups, I really wanted the reusable cups to work. Unfortunately, my DH had also invested in a tremendous amount of fine ground Illy espresso, which clogs up the K cup screens almost immediately. To get around this, I fill each of the three I purchased with a about half of a scoop and I use all three for one cup of coffee.

I plan to try them with some coarse ground coffee someday, and I expect I will revise this to a five star rating. Meanwhile, I'm taking apart my plastic k cups, composting the coffee (azalea's love coffee grounds, by the way), and washing and recycling the plastic and foil.
